2025 will close out with an Arctic front bringing snow squalls & much colder air from the Upper Midwest to the Northeast... while 2026 will ring in with heavy rain & mountain snow across the Southwest along with the risk of flashing flooding in southern California. Be safe!

Snowy & cold conditions are expected across the Northeast and Midwest, while heavy rain & storms bring a flood threat to the West esp. in SoCal.

Stay up to date by visiting weather.gov. Our dedicated team of meteorologists have you covered 24/7.

We hope you have a wonderful start to the new year.

Lake effect snow showers will continue through Saturday downwind of Lakes Erie, Ontario & eastern portions of Lake Superior.

A series of storm systems will continue to impact CA and the PacNW through the weekend into next week, bringing widespread rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds.
Elevated fire-weather conditions are expected across portions of west and southwest Texas as relative humidity values to fall into the 20s with winds in the 10-15 mph range with stronger gusts.

Another Atmospheric River event will impact the West Coast into the weekend bringing more rain and an isolated risk for flash flooding.

Heavier snow will also begin for the Sierra and higher mountains in the north of the state Saturday. Gusty winds and some coastal flooding can be expected as well.

Well above average conditions will continue over the Interior West and expand northward over the Plains in the next couple days. Forecast highs generally range from the 40s and 50s for the Interior West; the 50s and 60s for the High Plains, central Plains, and Southeast; and 70s and 80s for Texas.

Much above average temperatures stretch from the Interior West to the Plains and South while below average temperatures continue from the Midwest to the Northeast.

Visit weather.gov for the latest in your neck of the woods.

A deep upper-trough continues to bring Pacific moisture into much of California, bringing waves of showers and thunderstorms over the area. Repeating rounds of thunderstorms and heavy rainfall may cause scattered areas of flash flooding. Visit weather.gov for the latest.

Well above average temperatures will focus over the heart of the country through the next couple of days with some record-tying/breaking highs possible. How's it look in your neck of the woods this week? Visit weather.gov for the latest.

Deep moisture being drawn up from the south ahead of a developing cold core kona low will produce periods of heavy snow and ice over the summits Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea. The low is expected to weaken southwest of the islands Tuesday through mid-week.
